answer:
Use the `-j` or `--max-concurrency` flag with `promptfoo eval`. The docs describe it as "Maximum number of concurrent API calls" [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]. For example:

```powershell
promptfoo eval -c promptfooconfig.yaml --max-concurrency 1
```

The OSWorld guide uses the same flag in a run: "--max-concurrency 1" [promptfoo/site/docs/guides/evaluate-osworld-with-inspect.md]. The short form `-j 1` should work the same way, per the option table.

`promptfoo redteam run` accepts the same `-j, --max-concurrency` option for concurrent API calls [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]. The `promptfoo retry` command's `--max-concurrency` is described differently, as "Maximum number of concurrent evals" [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md], so it limits evals rather than individual API calls.

The provided context doesn't say whether a config-file setting or environment variable can cap concurrency, so I don't know that.
